newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up strongly, follows natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up strongly, follows natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended strongly higher Thursday following surging natural gas prices and robust Western physical power prices, industry sources said.
Although most traders said higher natural gas prices did not have a direct physical impact on electricity futures, they said there was a significant psychological impact.
"We hit new contract highs and that is partially related to natural gas, but we are also seeing strong daily (electricity) prices," said one Houston-based trader.

January California Oregon Border (COB) futures ended up $1.83 at $28.80 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $28.85, while February finished up $1.53 at $22.38 after hitting a new contract high of $22.40 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds finished between 10 and 50 cents higher, with most traded months hitting new contract highs.
January Palo Verde (PV) finished up $2.10 at $28.93 after hitting a new contract high of $29.00, while February closed up $1.15 at a new contract high of $22.90.
March was the only remaining PV month to trade, settling up 50 cents at a new contract high of $20.50 per MWh.
Over-the-counter January COB and PV was quoted at $28.00-29.00 on Thursday afternoon following the electricity futures contract closes.
January San Juan natural gas was talked at $3.45 per million British thermal units Thursday, sources said.
In spot trade, firm, peak California Oregon Border (COB) electricity for Friday delivery was assessed at $34.00-35.00 per megawatt hour (MWH), up from $33.00-34.00 on Wednesday.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Friday was quoted $29.00-30.00 per MWh, up from $27.00-28.00.
Traders said electricity futures could pull back from the highs on Friday if natural gas takes the lead lower, but said it is possible prices could continue to climb.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 850 COB and 99 PV contracts traded Thursday.
